subject: Post-incident summary — inference latency surge (Jul 18)
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@tilestream.com>
Cc: Carlos Ortega <carlos@tilestream.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Jul 2028 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-incident summary — inference latency surge (Jul 18)

Hi Samantha (and Carlos),

Thanks again for your patience while we completed our internal investigation. This message provides a concise summary of what happened on Jul 18, the measured impact to TileStream, our root cause analysis in plain terms, the short- and medium-term mitigations we’ve implemented, and the actions we’ve committed to. Attached are the detailed timeline CSV and trace appendix for your team to review.

Executive summary
- Impact window: Jul 18, 2028 08:14–08:48 PDT.
- Observable customer impact: elevated 95th/99th token latency on TileStream production routes; peak token latency increased ~4–6x for ~34 minutes. No data loss or model degradation.
- Service continuity: requests succeeded but experienced significant delays; we delivered fallbacks to a smaller model variant for ~12 minutes to keep throughput.

What we found (plain language)
- A combination of an autoscaler edge condition and a cascading KV-cache invalidation caused a temporary surge in cold-start-like paths. Specifically: a misconfigured autoscale cooldown allowed multiple GPU worker pools to simultaneously restart during a transient load spike, and a recent cache-key namespace change invalidated prefix caches for a subset of routes. The concurrent effect multiplied per-request overhead and increased scheduling contention.

Timeline (high level)
- 08:14 PDT — Monitoring alert: token latency > 2s on several TileStream routes.
- 08:16 — Traffic spike detected from client retries correlated with a third-party orchestration job.
- 08:20 — Autoscaler began replacing two worker groups; during replacement, cache invalidation propagated, causing more requests to rebuild KV state.
- 08:26 — Fallback policy activated: traffic routed to a compatible smaller model to preserve completion rates.
- 08:48 — Normal latency profile restored after autoscaler stabilized and cache warmed.

Immediate mitigations already applied
- Fixed autoscaler cooldown configuration to prevent simultaneous pool restarts (deployed 08:35 PDT).
- Scoped cache invalidation to affected namespaces only (deployed 08:40 PDT).
- Enabled temporary request-throttling guard for high-retry flows (08:28 PDT) to prevent retry amplification.

Committed follow-up actions (owner / ETA)
- Engineering: Add autoscaler canary gating and stronger invariants to prevent multi-pool restart windows (Marissa Cole / 2 weeks).
- Engineering: Implement stronger namespace-safe cache invalidation semantics and a compatibility shim for old prefixes (Marissa / 1 week).
- Product/Support: Deliver an incident artifact pack and curated traces for TileStream security/audit review (Neha / 48 hours — attached).
- Account: Review SLA credit eligibility and provide a proposed credit within 5 business days (Ben Carter / 5 business days).

What this means for TileStream
- We believe the changes above materially reduce the probability of recurrence. We will also include this scenario in the next monthly chaos exercise to validate the fixes.

Attachments: inference-surge-timeline.csv (detailed per-minute metrics), traces-appendix.pdf (selected spans and trace IDs), mitigation-patch.diff (dev preview).

I understand how disruptive latency bursts are for your customers. If you prefer, we can schedule a technical walkthrough next week with Marissa and our SREs to step through the traces and the patch.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor

Redwood Inference

Hi Samantha — quick answers and next steps:

1) Payload integrity: We verified at the transport layer that no request bodies were truncated or dropped. All requests received 200/2xx codes at ingress; the increased latency was due to downstream scheduling and cache rebuilds. The attached traces show end-to-end request/response sizes.

2) SLA credit methodology: Our standard practice is to compute credit proportional to the percentage of requests that exceeded the SLA target during the incident window for affected routes. Ben will prepare a proposed credit and the supporting computation by Tue EOD.

3) Third-party job ID: The orchestration job is internal to TileStream’s ingestion pipeline (as indicated by the traffic pattern). We observed increased retries from the TileStream agent IP block; we correlated timestamps but did not have a direct job ID from your side. If you can share your ingestion job IDs for Jul 18 08:00–09:00 PDT, Marissa can cross-reference.

Walkthrough: Tue 07/24 09:30 PDT works for our team, Marissa and I will join. Ben will send the invite.

Thanks — we’ll follow up with the credit proposal and a link to a read-only Drive folder for the traces.

Regards,
Neha

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@tilestream.com>, Carlos Ortega <carlos@tilestream.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Jul 2028 14:40:00 -0700
Subject: Technical appendix: mitigation details and prevention plan

Hi Samantha/Carlos — following up with a technical note on the root cause and the concrete changes we shipped. I’ve included the relevant trace IDs in the attached PDF and the patch summary in mitigation-patch.diff.

Technical summary (concise)- Root cause: autoscaler cooldown misconfiguration + cache namespace change. When two pools restarted concurrently, request routing repeatedly hit cold execution paths and caused KV-cache reconstructions for ~40% of requests during the peak, amplifying latency.
- Fixes shipped:
  * Autoscaler: added cross-pool leader election and serialized draining to avoid concurrent restarts; added metrics to alert on simultaneous restart counts (deployed 08:35 PDT).
  * Cache: changed invalidation from global namespace drop to targeted tombstone markers; added a compatibility shim that allows workers to recognize prior prefix formats for 14 days (deployed 08:40 PDT).
  * Fallbacks: extended canary rollout to include a lightweight latency-probing step before model fallback; this prevents unnecessary switchovers.

Preventive controls (what we will change in our SRE playbook)
- Formalize an autoscaler invariant: never allow >1 pool restart in a 10-minute window for the same service.
- Add unit and integration tests for cache-namespace migrations.
- Add a regression test in the chaos harness to simulate simultaneous restarts + cache migrations.

Operational artifacts provided
- Trace IDs: tile-req-7a2f3c, tile-req-7a2f4d, tile-req-7a2f91 (included in traces-appendix.pdf).
- Patch: mitigation-patch.diff contains the autoscaler gating and cache shim code (dev branch).
- Dashboard links: we’ve added a per-route incident dashboard to the shared Drive folder.

If you want, we can provide a lightweight runbook entry that your on-call team can use to recognize and escalate this specific pattern.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
